definitions.explanation: Doing or considering things separately, paying attention to each item rather than the whole.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}を{一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つ{解|と}く。
examples.english: Solve the problems one by one.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つ{丁寧|ていねい}に{確認|かくにん}してください。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{生徒|せいと}の{名前|なまえ}を{一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つ{呼|よ}んでいった。
examples.english: She called out each student's name one by one.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つの{経験|けいけん}が{自分|じぶん}を{成長|せいちょう}させてくれる。

notes:
Emphasizes treating items individually rather than as a group. Conveys care, thoroughness, or deliberate attention to each element. Often used when someone wants to stress the importance of not rushing or skipping over details.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つ{確認|かくにん}する: to check each one
- {一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つ{丁寧|ていねい}に: carefully, one at a time
- {一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つの{作業|さぎょう}: each task
- {一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つ{片付|かたづ}ける: to deal with things one by one

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一|いち}つずつ: one at a time — more neutral and less emphatic than {一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つ
- それぞれ: each; respectively — focuses on individual differences rather than sequential attention
- {個別|こべつ}に: individually — more formal and often used in business or official contexts

RELATED PATTERNS:
- The reduplication pattern extends to other counters: {一人一人|ひとりひとり} (each person), {一歩一歩|いっぽいっぽ} (step by step), {一日一日|いちにちいちにち} (day by day)
